dialogue.content: （こんばんは。19時からよろしくお願いします）
dialogue.English: (Good evening. I look forward to our 7 p.m. session.)

dialogue.content: (よろしくお願いします)
dialogue.English: (I look forward to it as well.)

dialogue.content: こんばんは、相談員です。お越し下さり、ありがとうございます。はじめに年齢、性別と今日の相談事の内容をお伺いします。
dialogue.English: Good evening, I'm the counselor. Thank you for coming. To begin, may I ask your age, gender, and what you would like to discuss today?

dialogue.content: 40歳、女性です子どもが悩んでいるようで、どうしていいかわかりません。
dialogue.English: I'm 40 years old and female. My child seems to be struggling with something, and I don't know what to do.

dialogue.content: はい、お子さんがお悩みというご相談ですね。それはご心配だと思います。
dialogue.English: I see, so you're concerned because your child is having a difficult time. That must be very worrying for you.

dialogue.content: お子さんの性別と学年をお伺いできますか？
dialogue.English: Could you tell me your child's gender and grade in school?

dialogue.content: 中学1年生の女の子です。
dialogue.English: She's a girl in her first year of middle school.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます、中一の娘さんなのですね。お子さんが悩みを抱えている様子ということですが、もう少し詳しくお話をお伺いできますか？
dialogue.English: Thank you. So your daughter is in her first year of middle school. You mentioned she seems to be carrying some worries—could you tell me a bit more about what’s been happening?

dialogue.content: 友達にいじめられているようで、先日泣いていました。
dialogue.English: It seems she's being bullied by her friends, and she was in tears the other day.

dialogue.content: そんなことがあったのですね。それはお母さんとして、ご心配になるのはごもっともです。
dialogue.English: I'm sorry to hear that. As a mother, it's completely understandable that you'd be worried.

dialogue.content: はい…
dialogue.English: Yes...

dialogue.content: おこさんは、お母さんに何かお話になりましたか？
dialogue.English: Has your daughter told you anything about what's happening?

dialogue.content: はい。友達に無視されるみたいです。
dialogue.English: Yes. She said it seems like her friends are ignoring her.

dialogue.content: 急になので、娘も理由がわからないみたいです。
dialogue.English: It happened all of a sudden, so my daughter doesn't seem to know why either.

dialogue.content: そうだったのですね。ご本人にも理由が分からない、というと突然無視され始めたような状態だったのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: I see. So, when you say she doesn't know the reason herself, does that mean they suddenly started ignoring her?

dialogue.content: 失礼しました、
dialogue.English: My apologies,

dialogue.content: 急に無視され始めたということなのですね。
dialogue.English: So, they just suddenly started ignoring her, is that right?

dialogue.content: はい。そうです
dialogue.English: Yes, that's right.

dialogue.content: なるほど・・・今、お子さんは夏休みに入ったかと思いますがどんなご様子ですか？
dialogue.English: I see... I believe your daughter is on summer break now. How has she been?

dialogue.content: 夏休みですが、部活があるので、部活には行っています。
dialogue.English: It's summer break, but she has club activities, so she has been going to them.

dialogue.content: 無視する子も同じ部活なので、行きたくないと思うのですが…
dialogue.English: The children who are ignoring her are in the same club, so I imagine she doesn't want to go...

dialogue.content: そうだったのですね、同じ部活の子に無視されて嫌な思いをしながらも頑張っていらっしゃるのですね。
dialogue.English: I see. So, even though she's feeling upset about being ignored by kids in the same club, she's still trying her best to go.

dialogue.content: よかったら、お子さんがどんな部活をなさっているか、教えて頂けますか？
dialogue.English: If you're comfortable sharing, could you tell me what kind of club your daughter is in?

dialogue.content: そうですね。無理して行っているのかもしれません。何でもきちんとやらないといけないと思うタイプなので。
dialogue.English: That's right. She might be forcing herself to go. She's the type of person who feels she has to do everything properly.

dialogue.content: 部活は吹奏楽部です。
dialogue.English: She's in the concert band.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。嫌な思いを抱えながらも部活に一生懸命いっていらっしゃるのですね。とても真面目で部活に熱心なのですね。
dialogue.English: Thank you. She's giving it her all at her club activities, even while carrying those difficult feelings. She sounds very conscientious and dedicated to the band.

dialogue.content: そうですね。真面目な子で、あまり気持ちもはっきり言えないので、心配です。
dialogue.English: That's right. She's a very earnest child and isn't very good at clearly expressing her feelings, so I'm worried.

dialogue.content: なるほど。嫌な事があってもあまり口には出さないタイプ、ということですね？お母さんが心配になるのは良く分かります。
dialogue.English: I see. So she's the type who doesn't say much even when things are unpleasant for her, is that right? I can certainly understand why you're worried.

dialogue.content: はい。そんなタイプです。どうしたら、いいでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Yes, that’s the type she is. What should I do?

dialogue.content: 少し話が戻りますが、お子さんがいじめにあっていることを気づかれたのは、いつ頃でしょうか？
dialogue.English: Going back a bit, when did you first notice that your daughter was being bullied?

dialogue.content: 1か月前くらいからです。
dialogue.English: About a month ago.

dialogue.content: とすると、お母さんはこの1ヶ月、気が気では無かったと思います。とてもしんどかったですね。
dialogue.English: In that case, I imagine you've been worried sick this past month. That must have been very difficult for you.

dialogue.content: はい…でも、娘の方がつらいと思うので
dialogue.English: Yes... but I think it's harder on my daughter.

dialogue.content: ええ、けれどお母さんがご心配で心を痛める気持ちも相当つらいのでは、とわたしは思います。
dialogue.English: Yes, but I imagine that the worry and heartache you feel as her mother is also incredibly difficult.

dialogue.content: この1ヶ月間、心配しながらずっと娘さんを見守っていらっしゃったのですね。お疲れではありませんか？
dialogue.English: You've been watching over your daughter with concern for this whole month. Aren't you feeling exhausted?

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。私は大丈夫です。
dialogue.English: Thank you. I'm okay.

dialogue.content: そうでしたか、とっても娘さん思いのお母さんですね。そんなお母さんがそばにいるから、娘さんも頑張って部活に行けているのかも知れないですね。
dialogue.English: I see. You're such a caring mother. Perhaps having you by her side is what gives your daughter the strength to keep going to her club activities.

dialogue.content: いえ…でも何も解決してあげれていません。どうしていいかもわからないし。
dialogue.English: No... but I haven't been able to resolve anything for her. I don't even know what to do.

dialogue.content: そうですね、確かに娘さんご本人のことなので、代わってあげることは出来ないですね。
dialogue.English: That's true. Since this is something your daughter is going through, you can't go through it for her.

dialogue.content: お母さんとしては、娘さんがどんな状態になったらいいな、と思われますか？もちろんいじめが無くなればそれに越したことはないと思いますが。
dialogue.English: As her mother, what do you hope for your daughter's situation? Of course, the best thing would be for the bullying to stop, but beyond that?

dialogue.content: もちろん、いじめがなくなることが一番ですが…少しでも学校が楽しくなってくれるといいと思います
dialogue.English: Of course, the most important thing is for the bullying to stop... but I hope school can become a little more enjoyable for her.

dialogue.content: 今は、無理して行っていると思うので…
dialogue.English: Because right now, I think she's forcing herself to go...

dialogue.content: そうですね。娘さんに、今お母さんが感じていらっしゃることをお伝えになったことはありますか？
dialogue.English: I see. Have you shared any of these thoughts with your daughter?

dialogue.content: 無理しなくてもいいことは伝えています。
dialogue.English: I have told her that she doesn't have to force herself.

dialogue.content: そうだったんですね。娘さんは、きっとその一言で安心出来ているのだと思いますよ。「お母さんがわかってくれてる」と。
dialogue.English: I see. I'm sure hearing that from you has helped her feel relieved, thinking, 'My mom understands.'

dialogue.content: そうなんでしょうか。
dialogue.English: Do you really think so?

dialogue.content: お母さんが「無理しなくて良い」と言ってくれているのに部活には行く。ということは、娘さんは部活がとても好きで、お母さんがついていると感じて心強いのではないでしょうか？
dialogue.English: She goes to her club activities even though you've told her, 'You don't have to force yourself.' Doesn't that suggest that she really likes her club, and perhaps she feels stronger knowing that you're on her side?

dialogue.content: ここまでお話をしてみて、いかがですか？
dialogue.English: How do you feel after talking through this so far?

dialogue.content: そうですね。部活に行かないと皆に迷惑かけるからって行っています。
dialogue.English: Yes. She says she has to go because otherwise she'd be letting everyone down.

dialogue.content: 責任感もお強いのですね、娘さんは。
dialogue.English: She has a strong sense of responsibility, doesn't she?

dialogue.content: 私の言葉が何か安心感になっているのであればいいと思いました。
dialogue.English: I hope that my words are providing her with some sense of reassurance.

dialogue.content: ちょっと自信はありませんが…
dialogue.English: Though I’m not very confident...

dialogue.content: そうですね。もし今後、いじめがひどくなって、娘さんの普段の様子が変わってきたら、きっとお母さんはお気づきになりますよね。
dialogue.English: I see. If the bullying were to get worse in the future and you saw a change in your daughter's usual demeanor, I'm sure you would notice, wouldn't you?

dialogue.content: はい。気づけるようにはしておきたいです。
dialogue.English: Yes. I want to be sure I'm able to notice.

dialogue.content: お母さんもとても娘さんを大事に思っていらっしゃり、とてもよく娘さんの事を見ていらっしゃるので、わたしは安心しています。
dialogue.English: You care so deeply for your daughter and are paying such close attention to her, so that puts my mind at ease.

dialogue.content: ですので、娘さんのお話をいつでも聞けるような心の準備をなさるというのもひとつかな、と思います。
dialogue.English: So, I think one good approach is to simply be mentally prepared to listen to your daughter whenever she wants to talk.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: そして、もし娘さんがまた泣きたくなるようなことがあったら、何があったのか、何がつらいの？とお話を聞いて、困ったらまたここへ相談に来て頂ければと思うのですが、いかがでしょうか？
dialogue.English: And if something happens again that makes your daughter feel like crying, you can listen to her and ask what happened and what's hurting her. And if you find yourself at a loss, I hope you'll feel you can come back here to talk. How does that sound?

dialogue.content: 話だけでも聴けるようにしておこうと思います。
dialogue.English: I'll make sure to at least be there to listen to her.

dialogue.content: そうですね、誰かに話せるというのはとても大事なことですよね。
dialogue.English: Yes, being able to talk to someone is a very important thing, isn't it?

dialogue.content: はい。その時はまたよろしくお願いします。
dialogue.English: Yes. If that happens, I look forward to speaking with you again.

dialogue.content: 娘さんにはお母さんが強い味方だと思います。ここまででお時間となってしまいますが、大丈夫でしょうか？
dialogue.English: I believe you are a strong ally for your daughter. That's all the time we have for today, is that okay?

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。はい。大丈夫です
dialogue.English: Thank you. Yes, that's fine.

dialogue.content: お世話になりました
dialogue.English: Thank you for your help.

dialogue.content: 大事なお話を聞かせて下さってありがとうございました。ここにはいつでも来て下さいね。終了のメッセージをお送りいたします。
dialogue.English: Thank you for sharing such an important matter with me. Please know you can come back anytime. I will now send the closing message.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: Thank you very much.
